Its fix information is the same; the package and affected versions differ. Background Jinja2 is a popular templating engine for Python, widely used for generating dynamic web content. It provides a flexible and secure way to render templates by separating logic from presentation. However, Jinja2 is vulnerable to HTML attribute injection when user input is passed as keys to the xmlattr filter. This filter accepts keys containing non-attribute characters, which can lead to the injection of additional attributes and potential cross-site scripting (XSS) attacks. Vulnerability Detail The xmlattr filter in Jinja2 allows keys with characters that are not valid in XML/HTML attributes. Since XML/HTML attributes cannot contain spaces, /, >, or =, these characters are interpreted as starting separate attributes. If an application accepts user input as keys and renders them in pages visible to other users, an attacker can exploit this vulnerability to inject malicious attributes and perform XSS attacks. The previous fix for CVE-2024-22195 only addressed spaces but not other characters. Accepting keys as user input is now considered an unintended use case of the xmlattr filter, and code that does so without validating the input is insecure. How To Fix Latest published version: 3.1.6 as of 23 Oct 2026 pip install --upgrade \"jinja2==3.1.6\" Upgrading to it may include breaking changes; the version below is the minimum fixed release for this vulnerability. However, developers can mitigate the risk by avoiding the use of user input as keys for the xmlattr filter.
